questions.stem: On Image color modes: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that an image intended for print is supplied in a light-based color mode. What should be checked before production begins?

options.text: That the image has the largest possible file size before printing
options.misconception: confuses file size with correctness of color mode

options.text: That the image is converted to the print model with a proper profile
That the image is renamed with the printer's required extension
options.misconception: mistakes the act of naming for an actual conversion

options.text: That the image is converted entirely to black and white
options.misconception: overcorrects by discarding all useful color information

questions.explanation: Images created in a light-based color mode can reproduce differently in print, so they should be converted to the print color model using an appropriate profile before production. Renaming or resizing a file does not change its color mode.
questions.hint: Does changing a file's name or size convert the colors within it?
